description: Phase 13 certified imported prior-provider history in the year-end settlement, including imported de minimis capped at its statutory ceilings. A worker whose previous provider's months are imported and whose later months the engine calculated can receive the same de minimis category from both sources. The statutory ceiling (RR 29-2025) applies once per category and statutory period to the worker, not once per source. Phase 14 certifies that the year-end settlement applies it to the union.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN, annual table effective 2023 onward: taxable income <= 250,000 exempt; to 400,000 at 15% over 250,000 (22,500 at 400,000); to 800,000 at 22,500 + 20% over 400,000.
sources.deMinimis: BIR RR 29-2025 de minimis ceilings in force for 2026 (the repository's DE_MINIMIS_2026 table): uniform and clothing allowance 8,000 a year; rice subsidy 2,500 a month. The part of a benefit inside its ceiling is exempt; the part above it is treated as other benefits.
sources.thirteenthMonthAndBenefits: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e) as amended by TRAIN: 13th-month pay and other benefits share one exemption of 90,000.
sources.sss: SSS 2025 contribution schedule: employee share 5% of the monthly salary credit; salary credit in steps of 500 (a month's compensation of 31,750-32,249.99 gives 32,000; 32,750-33,249.99 gives 33,000; 34,750 and above gives the 35,000 maximum). The engine computes SSS on the month's gross, de minimis included.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' statutory timing. The company switched provider on 2026-07-01: January to June are imported monthly rows (pay date = last day of the month), July to December (cutoffs 13-24) are calculated by the engine.

Each worker's basic pay is PHP 30,000 a month. An imported month: basic 30,000, SSS 1,500, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 200, withholding 1,007.40 (the previous provider's own contributions), plus the de minimis stated in the case, which raises its gross. A calculated cutoff: basic 15,000 plus half of the month's de minimis grant, PhilHealth 375, Pag-IBIG 100, SSS half of 5% of the month's salary credit.
The 13th month is the accrued basic of the year, 360,000 / 12 = 30,000, paid by nobody, so it is accrued in the settlement and joins the shared 90,000 pool.
Year-end annualization reads Released runs, so each calculated run is set to Released directly in the fixture.

Withholding during the calculated cutoffs is not asserted: only the settlement's own figures (gross, non-taxable, contributions, taxable income, tax due and the de minimis and benefit-pool breakdown) are, because that is what the shared ceiling changes.

ceilingPartlyUsedByPreviousProvider.description: Uniform allowance: previous provider 1,000 a month (6,000 in six months); engine grant 2,000 a month (12,000). Paid 18,000 against the 8,000 yearly ceiling: exempt 8,000, excess 10,000. Gross: imported 6 x 31,000 = 186,000 + calculated 12 x 16,000 = 192,000 + 13th month 30,000 = 408,000. Contributions: imported 6 x 2,450 = 14,700; calculated 6 x (SSS 5% of 32,000 = 1,600 + 750 + 200) = 15,300; 30,000. Benefit pool 30,000 + 10,000 = 40,000, all inside 90,000. Non-taxable 30,000 + 8,000 + 40,000 = 78,000. Taxable 330,000; tax 15% over 250,000 = 12,000.00.

ceilingExhaustedByBothSources.description: Uniform allowance: previous provider 6,000 a month (36,000); engine grant 6,000 a month (36,000). Paid 72,000 against the 8,000 yearly ceiling: exempt 8,000, excess 64,000. Gross: imported 6 x 36,000 = 216,000 + calculated 12 x 18,000 = 216,000 + 13th month 30,000 = 462,000. Contributions: imported 14,700; calculated 6 x (SSS 5% of the 35,000 maximum credit = 1,750 + 750 + 200) = 16,200; 30,900. Benefit pool 30,000 + 64,000 = 94,000: 90,000 exempt, 4,000 taxable. Non-taxable 30,900 + 8,000 + 90,000 = 128,900. Taxable 333,100; tax 15% over 250,000 = 12,465.00. Treating each source's ceiling on its own would exempt 16,000 and let the pool absorb 86,000: taxable 329,100, tax 11,865.00, 600.00 too little.

monthlyCeilingInSeparatePeriods.description: Rice subsidy (2,500 a month ceiling): previous provider 3,000 a month in January to June; engine grant 3,000 a month in July to December. The months never overlap, so each month has its own ceiling: 12 months x 2,500 exempt = 30,000, 12 x 500 = 6,000 excess. Gross: imported 6 x 33,000 = 198,000 + calculated 12 x 16,500 = 198,000 + 13th month 30,000 = 426,000. Contributions: imported 14,700; calculated 6 x (SSS 5% of 33,000 = 1,650 + 750 + 200) = 15,600; 30,300. Benefit pool 30,000 + 6,000 = 36,000, all inside 90,000. Non-taxable 30,300 + 30,000 + 36,000 = 96,300. Taxable 329,700; tax 15% over 250,000 = 11,955.00.

importedHistoryWithoutDeMinimis.description: The previous provider paid no de minimis; the engine grants uniform allowance 6,000 a month in July to December (36,000) against the 8,000 yearly ceiling. Nothing imported shares the ceiling, so the engine's own accounting stands: exempt 8,000, excess 28,000. Gross: imported 6 x 30,000 = 180,000 + calculated 12 x 18,000 = 216,000 + 13th month 30,000 = 426,000. Contributions: imported 14,700; calculated 6 x (1,750 + 750 + 200) = 16,200; 30,900. Benefit pool 30,000 + 28,000 = 58,000 inside 90,000. Non-taxable 30,900 + 8,000 + 58,000 = 96,900. Taxable 329,100; tax 15% over 250,000 = 11,865.00.

limitations: Only the year-end settlement is certified. The payroll engine still applies the ceiling to its own earlier cutoffs only, so in a provider-switch year its monthly payslip lines may show more of a category as exempt than the settlement finally allows, and its withholding during those cutoffs follows; the payroll run flags that combination for review and the settlement corrects the year. Withholding during the calculated cutoffs is therefore not asserted here.

Only fixed-peso ceiling categories are shared across sources. The daily overtime/night meal allowance (a wage-order based daily ceiling) and monetized leave days stay exactly as the engine accounted them.
Monthly imported rows only, one category per worker. Categories with a month, semester and year period are handled by the same rule; the month and year periods are exercised.
The release approval workflow and the HTTP, role and MFA gates are not exercised. The importer is covered by its own tests.
Whether SSS compensation should include de minimis benefits is a rule question for a practitioner; the expectations here follow the engine's current treatment (SSS on the month's gross).

The expected values are derived by hand from the cited BIR rules (TRAIN annual table, RR 29-2025 ceilings, the 90,000 exemption) and the repository's year-end treatment. The owner has decided that no separate Philippine tax practitioner review is required.
